summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of primary central nervous system lymphoma in remission and prior systemic lymphoma, was admitted for evaluation of dizziness and a fall two weeks prior. Initial CT head revealed new hypodensities in the left thalamus and cerebral peduncle, prompting an MRI which showed enhancing lesions concerning for possible lymphoma recurrence or treatment-related changes such as methotrexate toxicity. A spinal tap was performed with borderline elevated protein and elevated CSF b2-microglobulin, though cytology and flow remain pending. Cultures showed no growth. A full-body CT found no evidence of systemic lymphoma. He was managed supportively with a magnesium citrate dose for constipation and monitored for falls. He remained neurologically stable with no further episodes. Discharge was planned with follow-up to determine next steps, including possible PET scan or empiric treatment. He was discharged home in stable condition on his baseline medications.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
